rationale_one_line: Gallery (museum-white, IBM Plex Serif, blue accent) is the calm research-paper register that matches Nakajima's haiku-meets-systems voice; MANIFESTO punches the single thesis ('the log is the agent') with two flash beats, which earns the bold ActiveGraph claim without overselling 200 stars.
writing_tone_notes: Terse declarative cadence. Short sentences. Treat the reader as someone who already knows what an agent loop is. The triplet 'graph / behaviors / trace' is Yohei's own; let him keep two of the three (scenes), and put the third somewhere else (caption or close). No marketing adjectives. No exclamation. The video should feel like a Sunday-evening blog post he might have written himself.
do_rules: Caption opens with the handle and leads with the 200-star + arxiv-paper combo, then lands the BabyAGI lineage hook.
Scenes own the 'replay / fork / trace' mechanism vocabulary; caption owns 'deterministic / auditable / forkable' adjective vocabulary.
Close subtitle owns 'calmer hands, harder problem.' — do NOT echo it in the tweet or the why-this-one.
Camera moves: at least four distinct, with one orbit on the fix scene (3D depth around the central thesis).
Why-this-one covers the personal arc (NYC, Untapped Capital, 220-line while-true loop history); the caption stays on the project.
dont_rules: Do NOT say 'the log is the agent' verbatim in scene copy. Caption owns that phrase; scenes paraphrase via 'append / replay / fork' mechanics.
Do NOT cite v1.0 or any version number in the caption (growth metric only).
Do NOT repeat the Nakajima triplet ('graph is the world / behaviors are physics / trace is the proof') in full anywhere. Two of three across scenes is the limit.
Do NOT echo 'BabyAGI' more than once across caption and why-this-one combined; the close subtitle should not say BabyAGI at all.
Do NOT use em or en dashes, semicolons, question marks, or body colons anywhere in copy.
